s0.why: [1] measure of earthquake strength by Richter with Gutenberg, presented in 1935 paper; [2] later renamed local magnitude scale M_L

s1.why: [8] each whole number is a tenfold increase in measured amplitude; [9] about 31.6 times the energy

s2.why: [3] shortcomings led most authorities to other scales like M_w, while much of the news media still calls them Richter magnitudes

f0.why: [1] developed by Richter in collaboration with Gutenberg and presented in the 1935 paper

f1.why: [33] he specified the Wood-Anderson seismograph as the standard instrument

f2.why: [35] magnitude 0 shock gives maximum amplitude of 1 micrometre at 100 km

f3.why: [9] each increase of 0.2 is approximately a doubling of energy released

f4.why: [32] he wanted magnitude zero to be around the limit of human perceptibility

q1.why: [5] gives 3 to 5 as a hundredfold amplitude increase; [8] tenfold per whole number

q2.why: [31] logarithmic scale adopted to span the wide range of possible values; [5] logs make measurements manageable

q3.why: [31] tenfold-step scale similar to the astronomers' magnitude scale for star brightness, on Gutenberg's suggestion

q4.why: [40] values now are M_w but press reports them as Richter, even over 8 where Richter is meaningless; [3] agrees

q5.why: [12] intensity and ground effects depend on focus depth among other factors, not only magnitude

q6.why: [37] the instrument would become saturated by strong earthquakes and unable to record high values
